Materials

Balancing premium presentation and material choices

FORME Packaging editorialUpdated October 21, 20263 min read

Start with a suitable structure and a purposeful amount of material. Evaluate the complete pack, including inserts, coatings and closures, before making an environmental statement.

In this guideReduce avoidable space firstList the components separatelyReview decoration on the actual stockKeep evidence tied to the orderDiscuss your packaging →

Reduce avoidable space first

Review the arrangement before selecting the outside dimensions. An oversized box needs more paper, a larger insert and more storage volume. A compact layout can still feel spacious if the contents have clear visual order and enough access for removal.

Protection remains part of the brief. Removing a divider that prevents glass-to-glass contact can create product damage and replacement shipments. Test the filled pack and simplify components that do not contribute to protection, assembly or useful presentation.

List the components separately

Record the outer wrap, structural board, insert, ribbon, magnets, window and coating as distinct items. Ask what each component is made from and how it is attached. A paper exterior does not describe the composition of the whole package.

A paperboard insert may suit one product while another requires a different support. Compare alternatives using the actual product weight and shape. Where practical, design components so they can be separated without destroying the entire box.

Review decoration on the actual stock

Premium presentation can come from careful proportions, clean wrapping and a restrained printed design. A material swatch is often more informative than adding another decorative process. Ask to see the selected finish on the proposed stock.

Coatings, laminations, foil and adhesive combinations affect the pack beyond appearance. Request exact material information and locally relevant end-of-life guidance for the markets where the packaging will be used. Avoid treating a generic symbol as evidence for every version of a design.

Keep evidence tied to the order

  • Confirm the precise paper and insert specifications.
  • Ask which documents apply to the supplied material.
  • Review certificates for scope and validity before using claims.
  • Keep approved samples and material references with the order.
  • Check disposal instructions against the actual component mix.

Our certification area is reserved for documents supplied and verified for the business. Project-specific claims should be confirmed in writing before they appear on packaging or in marketing copy.
